facts.material: electronic PPG sensor with red/IR/green LEDs; textile bands; tablet
facts.function: continuous non-invasive monitoring of pulse rate and SpO2 (pulse oximetry) with Bluetooth transmission for parental/clinical review
facts.form: system imported with Gabi sensor, four textile bands, tablet with monitor app, cables, adapters, guides
facts.end_use: medical monitoring of children by parents and clinicians

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 9018 covers electro-diagnostic instruments and apparatus used in medical sciences, including apparatus for functional exploratory examination such as pulse oximeters
GRI 3(b): the Gabi sensor, which performs the measurement, gives the system its essential character; bands, tablet, cables and adapters are ancillary
GRI 6: 9018.19 other electro-diagnostic apparatus; 9018.19.95 other; 9018.19.95.50 other apparatus

rejected_alternatives.reason: the sensor is a complete apparatus, not a part or accessory
consumer wellness wearables go there; this device measures SpO2/pulse for medical monitoring and is covered by heading 9018
Bluetooth transmission is ancillary to the medical measuring function
the tablet is an accessory to the system; if CBP treats the items as not a set, the tablet would be classified separately

missing_facts: Whether CBP treats the tablet, chargers and adapters as a GRI 3(b) set with the sensor or classifies them separately
classification.rationale: The Gabi sensor is a wearable pulse oximeter that measures pulse rate and oxygen saturation by photoplethysmography for monitoring by parents and clinicians. CBP classifies pulse oximeters in 9018.19.95 as electro-diagnostic apparatus (H338599, in force). The sensor performs the core function and gives the system its essential character, so the system falls in 9018.19.95.50 (other apparatus).
